Pytest Unit Tests for LateFeeCalculator

The following test module exercises the early returns, weekday/weekend handling, grace-period boundary, minimum fee, prorated calculation, rounding, maximum cap, and constructor behavior. 

from datetime import date

import pytest

from late_fee_calculator import LateFeeCalculator


@pytest.fixture
def calculator():
    return LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2024, 1, 31))


def test_constructor_uses_explicit_today():
    today = date(2024, 5, 1)

    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=today)

    assert calculator._today == today


def test_constructor_uses_current_date_when_today_is_omitted(monkeypatch):
    expected = date(2024, 5, 1)

    class FakeDate:
        @classmethod
        def today(cls):
            return expected

    monkeypatch.setattr("late_fee_calculator.date", FakeDate)

    calculator = LateFeeCalculator()

    assert calculator._today == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "start,end,expected",
    [
        (date(2024, 1, 10), date(2024, 1, 10), 0),
        (date(2024, 1, 11), date(2024, 1, 10), 0),
        (date(2024, 1, 12), date(2024, 1, 15), 1),
        (date(2024, 1, 13), date(2024, 1, 16), 2),
        (date(2024, 1, 13), date(2024, 1, 15), 1),
    ],
)
def test_weekday_days_between(calculator, start, end, expected):
    assert calculator._weekday_days_between(start, end) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize("balance", [0, -1, -500])
def test_non_positive_balance_has_no_fee(calculator, balance):
    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(
        balance, date(2024, 1, 1)
    ) == 0


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "due_date",
    [
        date(2024, 1, 31),  # No elapsed days.
        date(2024, 1, 19),  # Exactly 10 weekdays.
        date(2024, 1, 20),  # Weekend-inclusive boundary still at grace.
    ],
)
def test_no_fee_during_grace_period(calculator, due_date):
    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(10_000, due_date) == 0


def test_weekends_are_excluded_from_days_past_due():
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2024, 1, 22))

    # Friday Jan 12 through Monday Jan 22 contains six weekdays.
    assert calculator._weekday_days_between(
        date(2024, 1, 12), date(2024, 1, 22)
    ) == 6

    # Six weekdays are within the ten-day grace period.
    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(
        10_000, date(2024, 1, 12)
    ) == 0


def test_minimum_fee_applies_after_grace_period():
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2024, 1, 31))

    # Jan 1 through Jan 31 has 22 weekdays; 12 are billable.
    # Raw fee is 10,000 * .015 / 30 * 12 = 60 cents.
    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(10_000, date(2024, 1, 1)) == 500


def test_prorated_fee_is_calculated_in_whole_cents():
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2024, 1, 31))

    # 100,000 cents, 12 billable weekdays:
    # 100000 * .015 / 30 * 12 = 600 cents.
    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(100_000, date(2024, 1, 1)) == 600


def test_rounding_is_half_up():
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2024, 1, 16))

    # Jan 1 through Jan 16 has 11 weekdays, so one billable day.
    # 1,000 cents * .015 / 30 = 0.5 cents, rounded to 1 cent,
    # then raised to the $5 minimum.
    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(1_000, date(2024, 1, 1)) == 500


def test_maximum_fee_cap_applies():
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2025, 1, 1))

    # A long overdue invoice produces a fee greater than 25%.
    balance = 100_000
    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(balance, date(2020, 1, 1)) == 25_000


def test_minimum_fee_is_returned_when_cap_is_below_minimum():
    calculator = LateFeeCalculator(today=date(2024, 1, 31))

    # The implementation applies max(capped, MIN_FEE_CENTS), so the minimum
    # fee wins even when 25% of the balance is below $5.
    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(1_000, date(2024, 1, 1)) == 500


def test_fee_is_not_charged_for_future_due_date(calculator):
    assert calculator.compute_fee_cents(
        100_000, date(2024, 2, 1)
    ) == 0

Coverage

These tests cover every conditional branch in the supplied implementation, including both outcomes of the balance check, date-range check, grace-period check, and the cap/minimum fee paths. Run them with: 

pytest --cov=late_fee_calculator --cov-branch --cov-report=term-missing
Implementation note: the supplied code returns the $5 minimum even when the 25% maximum cap is below $5. The test test_minimum_fee_is_returned_when_cap_is_below_minimum documents that exact behavior.
